description: Behaviour vectors of the layers above the relay (``protocol_spec.md`` section 16.3).

cases.name: hello_at_half_an_interval_then_every_interval
cases.description: The first HELLO at a random point of the first interval (midpoint 30 s), then every hello_interval ±15 % (midpoint 60 s); TARGET 0xFF, never repeated.

cases.name: silent_neighbour_reported_lost_and_acknowledged
cases.description: A neighbour silent for more than miss_limit (5) intervals is reported LOST after report_delay; the controller's REPLY ends it.

cases.name: unacknowledged_report_repeated_then_abandoned
cases.description: A REPORT nobody acknowledges goes again every report_timeout (15 s), report_retries (3) more times, then is dropped.

cases.name: report_suppressed_by_another_nodes_report
cases.description: Another node's REPORT about the same subject and event heard during report_delay cancels ours.

cases.name: neighbour_heard_again_reported_recovered
cases.description: A neighbour reported LOST that is heard again is reported RECOVERED (a new sequence).

cases.name: flap_before_the_report_cancels_it
cases.description: Heard again before its LOST report went out: LOST and RECOVERED cancel, nothing is reported.

cases.name: weak_neighbour_silent_not_reported
cases.description: A neighbour whose smoothed RSSI is below watch_rssi (−118.5 dBm), heard for less than weak_window intervals, is never reported.

cases.name: weak_neighbour_watched_by_its_hello_rate
cases.description: A weak neighbour known for weak_window (10) intervals or more is watched on a longer fuse: LOST once silent for the least n with (1 − rate)ⁿ ≤ 1e-4, the rate (HELLOs after the first over the intervals since, the silence included) falling while it stays silent; heard every other interval for 40 min, n settles at 26.

cases.name: full_table_forgets_the_least_recently_heard
cases.description: With the table full (max_neighbours, 2 here), a new neighbour replaces the one heard least recently (not the one first heard), which is then never reported.

cases.name: smoothed_rssi_decides_who_is_watched
cases.description: The watch threshold applies to the smoothed RSSI (EWMA, new HELLO weight 0.25): −115 then −125 dBm smooth to −117.5, above watch_rssi, so its silence is reported.

cases.name: weak_neighbour_rate_ignores_the_time_asleep
cases.description: Woken, a weak neighbour's start moves on with its last HELLO (resume): its rate counts awake intervals only, so it is watched and reported LOST after 9 intervals; counted over the 29 min asleep, its rate would be too low to watch (n > max_miss).

cases.name: join_after_half_the_spread_and_acknowledged
cases.description: JOIN at a random point of join_spread (midpoint 15 s), WIN join_window; the gateway's routed REPLY echoing its id ends it.

cases.name: unanswered_join_backs_off_with_fresh_ids
cases.description: Unanswered, JOIN again with a new message id after join_backoff, doubling from 30 s up to 300 s.

cases.name: another_join_holds_ours
cases.description: join_quiet: another node's JOIN heard pushes ours back by 3 s plus as much again at random (midpoint 4.5 s).

cases.name: scan_answered_along_its_path_with_neighbours
cases.description: A DISCOVER is answered once, after its window and at a random point of its SPREAD, back along its path; neighbours are the scan copies' senders and the HELLO table's strongest, not the parent; the answer stands in for the JOIN.

cases.name: boot_in_a_sleeping_network_sends_a_wake_join
cases.description: Q22: a node booting dormant stays awake for join_spread + window + 15 s, its JOIN in that time is a wake JOIN (PROBE_WAKE, long preamble); then it samples.

cases.name: wake_net_wakes_for_its_lease_then_samples
cases.description: A WAKE_NET wakes a dormant node until its LEASE (paid from the awake budget); it is relayed with the long preamble; the node samples again once the lease is over and the relay has nothing left.

cases.name: sleep_net_ends_the_lease
cases.description: SLEEP_NET ends the lease at once; the node passes it on first.

cases.name: fourth_wake_within_the_period_refused
cases.description: At most max_wakes (3) WAKE_NET per wake_period (60 s) are honoured; the fourth neither wakes nor is relayed.

cases.name: awake_budget_cuts_the_lease
cases.description: WAKE_NET leases draw on net_awake_quota (20 s here): the lease is cut to what is left, and with nothing left the next is refused.

cases.name: keepalive_through_the_node_holds_it_awake
cases.description: A routed KEEPALIVE through the node holds it awake for the keepalive's LEASE + hold (5 s) past the network lease.

cases.name: wake_probe_wakes_for_its_window
cases.description: A wake probe (PROBE_WAKE) wakes the node for its window + probe_hold (3 s); it is passed on with the long preamble.

cases.name: woken_neighbour_table_resumes
cases.description: Silence while dormant is not silence: woken, every neighbour counts as heard at the wake-up, and the first HELLO goes within one interval.

cases.name: event_raised_dormant_goes_out_once_woken
cases.description: A module event raised while dormant waits; woken, it goes out within wake_spread (midpoint 15.5 s) and its REPLY ends it; it shares the REPORTs' sequence counter.
